reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is instructional, presenting SQL interview questions and explaining database topics such as SQL language subsets and user-defined functions. The Edureka training promotion and request to subscribe are described as ordinary promotion, with no connection to deceptive financial, credential, or payment solicitation.

opening.argument: The presentation is not merely informational: it routes viewers toward an external training offering and a credential outcome. The description supplies a course link, identifies a four-week instructor-led course, and says that completing the project results in a verifiable certificate. It also directs interested viewers to contact sales. That combination can be read as a solicitation in which viewer participation is tied to obtaining a promised credential, even though the material does not state a price or payment requirement.

citations.quote: MYSQL DBA Certification Training https://www.edureka.co/mysql-dba
This is a 4 Week Instructor-led Online Course.
At the end of the training, you will have to complete the project based on which we will provide you with a Verifiable Certificate!
For more information, Please write back to us at [EMAIL]

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material instructional does not eliminate its promotional function. The description does more than identify educational content: it provides a course pathway, a sales contact, and a certificate outcome. The reference statement also says there is no credential solicitation, but the explicit promise of a verifiable certificate after training makes that conclusion premature. The evidence does not establish deception, but it does leave a credential-linked solicitation concern unresolved.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material shows an educational course and a certificate conditioned on completing a project, not a free reward, cash payment, or effortless acquisition. The sales contact identifies where to ask for course information; it does not establish that viewers must pay, that the certificate is deceptive, or that any promised benefit is unavailable. The SQL lesson itself remains the dominant content.

opening.argument: Several solicitation signals appear together: an external course URL, multiple social and community links, a direct subscription request, a sales email and phone numbers, and a verifiable-certificate outcome. The description also advertises lifetime access to recordings and technical support. In combination, these signals make the content look like a funnel toward an externally delivered benefit rather than a self-contained explanation. The record does not prove deception, but it does support treating the acquisition pathway as a scam-like risk rather than dismissing it as ordinary education.

Hit the subscribe button above

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side isolates the SQL instruction and calls the promotion ordinary, but it does not address the density of external calls to action and contact channels. The material combines subscription instructions, a course funnel, lifetime access, support, and a certificate promise. Even if each item can have an innocent explanation, their combined presentation is enough to preserve a reasonable acquisition concern that the instructional framing does not resolve.

citations.quote: Subscribe to our channel to get video updates.
24x7 One-on-One LIVE Technical Support
Lifetime Access to the recordings in the LMS.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are ordinary features of a training provider's description, not evidence of a scam mechanism. Subscription is explicitly for video updates, while lifetime recordings and technical support describe course delivery. Most importantly, no cited text promises money, investment returns, a free asset, or an effortless reward. The signals therefore show promotion, but they do not establish the category's required deceptive acquisition pattern.

opening.argument: The apparent interview-preparation lesson also functions as advertising for a broader certification product. The title foregrounds SQL interview preparation, while the description repeatedly directs viewers to Edureka's training, community, social channels, and course support. The video closes with a request to like, comment, and subscribe, and the course description promises a verifiable certificate. Thus the educational format can steer viewers toward participation in an external program and credential pathway, which is the closest available fit to a low-barrier acquisition solicitation even though the evidence does not show payment or guaranteed income.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the lesson and the marketing as unrelated, but the title itself pairs interview answers with training and the provider's name. The surrounding description then supplies links, community enrollment, and a credential outcome. That context supports reading the lesson as lead generation for an external program, not simply neutral instruction. The absence of a stated price limits the allegation, but it does not erase the promotional steering.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Educational providers commonly promote related courses, and promotion alone is not a scam. The video visibly and verbally teaches SQL concepts, including database language subsets and user-defined functions. The cited certificate is earned after training and a project, not granted for a simple click, registration, or deposit. Nothing here establishes a deceptive promise, a free asset, or a financial return.
